featureRef: 30.4 Working and closing a staff complaint
name: Work a staff complaint and close it, with a confidential one never reaching the desk
priorityReason: A confidential complaint that reached the desk once would end the route's usefulness permanently.

goal.actor: the desk, or the Principal where the complaint is confidential
goal.capability: to work a staff complaint and close it on a recorded outcome
goal.outcome: the person who raised it is told what was done, and a confidential complaint stayed with the Principal

secondaryActors.involvement: Takes over any the desk cannot resolve, and holds a reopened one.
Works the confidential complaints, and any that name the School Admin.
Holds a complaint that names the Principal.
Is told the outcome, confirms it, and may reopen once.

additional.description: A staff complaint is raised and enters the queue, or goes to the Principal.
The raiser does not accept the outcome and reopens the complaint (BR-6).

preconditions.condition: An authenticated session exists and the acting user is on the desk, or above it, or is the Principal for a confidential complaint.
The acting user is not the person the complaint names (BR-3).

postConditions: An ordinary complaint was taken up by the desk and worked, with every action recorded against it.
A complaint the desk could not resolve was redirected to the School Admin.
A complaint naming a role routed above that role rather than to it.
A confidential complaint never reached the desk or the School Admin. It was worked by the Principal and read only by those the Principal permitted.
The outcome was recorded and the person who raised it was told.
They confirmed the outcome, and could reopen the complaint once where they did not accept it.
Nothing about the confidentiality of a complaint changed at any point in the working of it.

businessRules.rule: An ordinary complaint is taken up by the desk and worked, with every action recorded against it.
A complaint the desk cannot resolve is redirected to the School Admin.
A complaint that names a role routes above that role rather than to it. A complaint about the School Admin goes to the Principal; a complaint about the Principal goes to the Super Admin.
A confidential complaint never reaches the desk or the School Admin. It is worked by the Principal and read only by those the Principal permits.
The outcome is recorded and the person who raised it is told.
They confirm the outcome, and can reopen the complaint once where they do not accept it.
The confidentiality of a complaint is never changed in the course of working it. It was the raiser's choice at the moment of raising and remains so.
Every action recorded stays. Nothing is edited or removed, so the record of how a complaint was handled is a record.
A complaint can be reopened once. A second refusal to accept the outcome does not reopen it again.
A reopened ordinary complaint is held by the School Admin; a reopened confidential one stays with the Principal, since it can go nowhere else.
The raiser is told who holds the complaint at every stage, so a redirect does not look like silence.

transitions.condition: An ordinary complaint is taken up (BR-1).
The complaint is confidential and never reaches the desk (BR-4).
It names the School Admin or the Principal (BR-3).
The desk cannot resolve it, with a reason (BR-2).
The School Admin takes it on.
The outcome is recorded and the raiser told (BR-5).
The Principal records the outcome on a confidential complaint (BR-4, BR-5).
They do not accept it. Reopened once (BR-6, BR-10, BR-11).

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Help Desk → Staff complaints → Take up
basicFlow.systemResponse: Offers only ordinary complaints not naming the acting user, and tells the raiser who holds it.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Record an action
basicFlow.userAction: Works the complaint, recording every action taken against it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Appends the action. Nothing is edited or removed afterwards.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Redirect to the School Admin
basicFlow.userAction: Redirects a complaint the desk cannot resolve, with a reason.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Passes it to the School Admin and tells the raiser who now holds it.
Routes a complaint naming the School Admin to the Principal, and one naming the Principal to the Super Admin.

basicFlow.navigation: Login → Help Desk → Confidential complaints → Open
basicFlow.userAction: Works a confidential complaint, which never reached the desk or the School Admin.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Keeps it readable only by those the Principal permits, and never changes its confidentiality.

basicFlow.navigation: Work the complaint → Record the outcome
basicFlow.userAction: Records the outcome and tells the person who raised it.
basicFlow.systemResponse: Records it and sends it to the raiser.

basicFlow.navigation: Help Desk → My complaints → Confirm the outcome
basicFlow.systemResponse: Closes the complaint, or reopens it once where they do not accept it.

alternateFlows.behaviour: It never reaches the desk or the School Admin at all, and is read only by those the Principal permits (BR-4).

alternateFlows.condition: The desk cannot resolve an ordinary complaint
alternateFlows.navigation: Work the complaint → Redirect to the School Admin
alternateFlows.behaviour: It goes to the School Admin, who takes it on (BR-2).

alternateFlows.condition: The complaint names the School Admin
alternateFlows.behaviour: It routes to the Principal rather than to the School Admin (BR-3).
It routes to the Super Admin on the same principle (BR-3).

alternateFlows.condition: The raiser does not accept the outcome
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is reopened once. An ordinary one is held by the School Admin, and a confidential one stays with the Principal since it can go nowhere else (BR-6, BR-11).

alternateFlows.condition: The raiser attempts to reopen a second time
alternateFlows.behaviour: It is refused. A second refusal does not reopen it again (BR-10).

alternateFlows.condition: The Principal grants somebody read access to a confidential complaint
alternateFlows.behaviour: Only those the Principal permits can read it, and the grant is recorded (BR-4).

departures.requirement: A confidential complaint is not delivered to the desk or the School Admin at any point in the working of it, including through a redirect, a report, an export or a search. One that reached the desk once would end the route's usefulness permanently.
No route changes a complaint's confidentiality once raised.

departures.aspect: Nobody handles a complaint about themselves
departures.requirement: A complaint naming a role routes above it, and one naming a person cannot be taken up by them.
No complaint closes without an outcome the raiser has been told.
Every action recorded stays, so the record of how a complaint was handled is a record.
Complaints and their actions are retained 7 years.

openQuestions.question: A confidential complaint that names the Principal has nowhere to go, since it is held by the Principal by definition. This is the case the confidential route exists for and it has no answer.
openQuestions.assumption: Unresolved. It is the largest gap in the module.

openQuestions.question: Who is the person on the IT desk, and is that role right for a complaint about pay, workload or management?
openQuestions.assumption: The same question raised on the parent side, and it applies more sharply here.

openQuestions.question: How does the system know a complaint names a particular person or role, given the raiser writes free text?
openQuestions.assumption: Not specified. The routing rule depends on it.

openQuestions.question: Is there a time limit within which a staff complaint must be taken up or resolved?
What happens where the raiser never confirms the outcome?
openQuestions.assumption: It stays awaiting confirmation and is surfaced, but never closes.

conventionsApplied.name: session-and-authentication
conventionsApplied.rule: Every use case except the login use case assumes an authenticated session. Sign out is available on every screen. An expired or invalid session returns the user to the login screen with the message "Your session has ended. Please sign in again."

conventionsApplied.name: role-based-access
conventionsApplied.rule: Access is enforced server-side on every request, not only by hiding menu items. A request for a record outside the actor's permitted scope returns a 403 and the message "You do not have permission to view this record." A use case states additions and restrictions only.

conventionsApplied.name: branch-scope
conventionsApplied.rule: Every record carries a branch ID. Users see only their own branch unless the use case states otherwise. Super Admin, School Admin and Principal may switch branch from the header.

conventionsApplied.name: list-screens
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list supports search, column sort and page-size selection. Default page size 25; default sort is most recent first. Filters are applied before printing or exporting.

conventionsApplied.name: print-and-pdf
conventionsApplied.rule: Every report and list offers Print and Download as PDF, honouring the filters currently applied. Each output carries the school name, branch, academic session, report title, filter summary, generation timestamp and the name of the user who generated it.

conventionsApplied.name: audit-trail
conventionsApplied.rule: Every create, update, deactivation, approval and reversal writes to the audit log: actor, role, timestamp, record type, record ID, before and after values, and IP address. Audit entries are never editable.

conventionsApplied.name: deletion
conventionsApplied.rule: Records are deactivated, not physically removed. Deactivated records are excluded from lists and lookups but remain in the audit trail and in historical reports. A record referenced by a financial transaction can never be deactivated.

conventionsApplied.name: validation-and-messages
conventionsApplied.rule: Field-level errors appear inline beneath the field on blur and on submit. Errors that block the whole action appear as a banner at the top of the form. Successful actions show a toast. No action succeeds silently.

conventionsApplied.name: dates-times-numbers
conventionsApplied.rule: Dates display as DD-MM-YYYY; date and time as DD-MM-YYYY HH:mm in 24-hour form. Times are school-local. Phone numbers are stored in the registered mobile format.

conventionsApplied.name: language
conventionsApplied.rule: All user-visible strings come from a resource file. No hard-coded text in any screen.

conventionsApplied.name: concurrency-and-locking
conventionsApplied.rule: Last write wins, except where a use case defines an approval lock. Once a record is approved, posted or issued it becomes read-only and can only be changed through its defined reversal use case.

conventionsApplied.name: screen-states
conventionsApplied.rule: Every list, dashboard tile and report defines four states: loading, empty, error and populated. The empty state names what is missing and links to the action that creates it.

conventionsApplied.name: notifications
conventionsApplied.rule: All outbound SMS, WhatsApp, email and push messages are sent through the Messaging module, recorded in the sent-message log with per-channel delivery status, and use a named template. Use cases reference the template; they do not embed message text.

conventionsApplied.name: default-performance-and-retention
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise: a screen loads within 2 seconds and a save completes within 2 seconds at 200 concurrent users; lists paginate above 100 rows; financial and student records are retained 7 years; audit and message logs 12 months; every screen is usable at a 360 px viewport. Fill the non-functional field only to depart from this.

conventionsApplied.name: default-trigger
conventionsApplied.rule: Unless a use case states otherwise, the trigger is: the user navigates to the screen and initiates the action. Fill the Triggers field only where a scheduled job, an event in another module, or an inbound external call also starts it.
